title: Johnny Dodds as favorite clarinetist
summary: Dodds was his favorite clarinetist. He heard him in Chicago, and describes his unusual High Society solo that started from the top. He mentions King Oliver's band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Who was your favorite clarinetist of all of the old time men that you heard when you were a boy? Who did you like best? I liked Johnny Dawson's best. You got to hear Johnny Dawson?

Yeah. That was my favorite one. He was. Johnny Dawson. I knew him in Chicago. He was wonderful then, I thought. Mm-hmm. Used to play here, man. I'd run. Got to hear that bamboo I'd love to hear that man play playing. I noticed you sound, sometimes, some of the things you do sound quite a bit like that. Yeah, I used to listen to him so much. I used to listen to the dots all the time. I'd love to hear that man play. What was it, can there anything special you can say about his playing, particularly your life? Now here's a number I used to love to hear him play. I used to love to hear him play High Society. I used to love to hear Johnny Dutch play High Society. He played High Society different from any other client that I've heard. Different from PQ and all them clients that played. He played High Society different. He never just started from his low notes down here. He started from the top with High Society. He thought when he hit that note, he said, Then he fall down. Then he come right back up again, you see. High Society, you see. And he played that, and that's what I used to like. Who was playing with him in his band? That was his band, was it? Johnny Dutch Band of the Roof Garden? Yeah, Joe Oliver. King Oliver. Oh, was Oliver's band? Yeah. King Oliver was playing. Who else was with him besides Oliver and Doug's? Well, I didn't know them fellas. See, I was young then. Johnny Dutch was the one I used to keep up with, because he was playing the clarinet. He was your favorite. Yeah, he was a lot of favorite, yeah. And those buck-eyed, him and buck-eyed. Of course, I never really care much about the connex, but I was crazy about that clarinet.
